newsitem.title: USA: New crop soybeans end down on favorable weather.
newsitem.headline: New crop soybeans end down on favorable weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed Thursday, with new crop months under pressure from favorable growing forecasts, traders said.
"There was pressure all day on new crop because of the weather," said Victor Lespinasse, floor trader with Dean Witter brokerage in Chicago.
July had been sharply higher for most of the session on short-covering gains, but a wave of bear-spreading near the close trimmed advances late, floor traders said.
"Lind-Waldock was bear-spreading aggressively on the close and he had more to do," said one floor trader.
Thursday's choppy tone in old crop July was also prompted by positioning before options expiration Friday at 1201 CDT.
The market typically gravitates toward the most active strike price at expiration, and some see that price as $8.25 per bushel in July.
Weather forecasts for the U.S. Midwest show scattered showers and summer-like warm weather. High temperatures are forecast to range from 73 to 90 degrees Fahrenheit.
CBOT July soybeans settled up 5-1/2 cents per bushel at $8.38 per bushel, and other months closed down six cents to 1/2 cent higher.
Export sales were largely within trade expectations and considered mildly supportive to prices, traders said.
USDA on Thursday said U.S. net sales of old crop soybeans during the week ended June 12 totaled 65,800 tonnes, above expectations for none to 50,000.
New crop sales totaled 264,300 tonnes, which was near the low end of expectations for 250,000 to 400,000 tonnes.

Most in the trade are looking for the National Oilseed Processors Association to show a slight decline in the pace of the weekly crush. Estimates ranged from 24.02 to 25.50 million bushels. Those figures compared with last week's pace of 25.378 million bushels.
On the day, ADM sold two million bushels July. ABN Amro Chicago Corp sold five million November and bought three million July and Merrill Lynch bought 2.5 million July, pit sources said.
In options trade, Refco bought 400 August $9.00 calls and sold 400 August $9.50 calls. Continental Grain bought 400 August $8.00 calls and bought 400 August $7.50 puts.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 58,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 66,709 contracts.
